note_text:
Patient is a 58-year-old woman referred for urologic evaluation of urinary frequency, urgency, and intermittent incomplete bladder emptying over the past four months. History was obtained noting no prior pelvic surgery, no hematuria, and no recent UTIs. Physical exam performed: abdomen soft, non-tender, no suprapubic fullness; pelvic exam without significant prolapse; neurologic exam of lower extremities grossly intact with normal perineal sensation and anal tone. Urinalysis with microscopy obtained in clinic today: negative for leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and blood; microscopy showed 0-2 WBC/hpf, no bacteria, no casts - no evidence of infection.

Given the persistence of voiding symptoms despite a benign initial workup, urodynamic studies are being ordered to clarify the etiology of her dysfunction (detrusor overactivity vs outlet obstruction vs impaired contractility) and to guide subsequent management, which may include medication adjustment or referral for further intervention. Plan is for a focused study including uroflowmetry, filling cystometry, and pressure-flow analysis only - no additional testing beyond what is needed to characterize her voiding pattern will be performed.

She was counseled on the procedure, risks, and expected findings. Will schedule urodynamics in the next 2-3 weeks and follow up with results to determine further plan of care.
